findings.statement: Obligation 1 (atomically bind one spawned agent_id to one run, assignment, and digest) is DISCHARGED on HEAD 4305533, established by my own reproduction rather than by reading the writer's numbers. (a) RACE CLOSED: I built 60 independent fixture trees, each with two assignments minted through the real `admit_agent.py --agent-id-unknown` (the mode in which no mint-time agent guard is constructible), one agent_id holding both tokens, and two SubagentStop processes started before either was read. Breaches (more than one `consumed` row): 0/60. The same probe against a mirror whose ONLY edit was replacing `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` with `pass`: 28/60 breaches (47%). The lock, not chance, is what closes it; my probe is therefore a detector, not a hope. (b) EVERY CONSUMING PATH IS INSIDE THE LOCK, by construction not by inspection luck: `consumed` is written at exactly three sites in .codex/hooks and .agent-harness/scripts -- subagent_stop_validate.py:698 (ledger row), :716 (receipt state) and :741 (lease state) -- and all three lie inside `consume_under_agent_lock` (defined :370, body ends :751), which `main` calls only at :349 inside `try/finally: os.close(lock_fd)` (:348-367), the lock having been acquired at :330 BEFORE the `conflicting_agent_assignment` read it guards (:402). No other module in the tree writes an admission receipt or appends a consume row; `admit_agent.py` only ever writes `state: "open"`. (c) LOCK-FAILURE HANDLING IS FAIL-CLOSED IN ALL SHAPES: symlinked lock dir, mkdir OSError, O_NOFOLLOW open OSError, non-BlockingIOError flock OSError and ftruncate/write OSError all return `(None, msg)` and reach `block(...)` at :331-338; pure contention returns `(None, "")` and blocks at :339-347. Mutation M3 (force `lock_error = ''`, i.e. treat an unusable lock as a skip) was killed by test_agent_lock_directory_failure_is_fail_closed and test_planted_symlink_at_the_agent_lock_path_blocks. (d) THE PER-RUN SCOPE IS HONESTLY STATED, not silently assumed: the lock key is (bound_run, agent_id) (:56-62), the Stop-time conflict read is scoped to run_dir/ADMISSIONS.jsonl (:402-403), the block text says 'One agent_id may consume at most one assignment per run (D-065 obligation 1)', admit_agent.py's guard is scoped to `harness/admissions/<run>` (:487-503), validate_harness.check_one_agent_one_assignment is invoked per run directory (:918), and test_one_agent_bound_in_one_run_is_still_admissible_in_another fixtures cross-run rebinding as DELIBERATE with a docstring saying so in as many words. The digest half of the obligation is carried by three independent pins I checked on live bytes: the Start lease's assignment_digests vs recomputed assignment sha (:436-449), the receipt's assignment_sha256 (:484-489), and the consume row's result_sha256 + assignment_sha256 (:698-715). SCOPE I AM NOT CLAIMING: an agent_id may legitimately hold one assignment in each of several runs; and `admit_agent.py --reopen` does not take the consume lock, so a reopen concurrent with an in-flight stop for the same assignment is a race the lock does not cover -- it is named in that script's own stderr warning, and it is a parent-operated tool, not an agent-reachable path.
assumptions_used: The 13-hour integration running on this host adds background load; it changes race timing but not the direction of the result (0/60 with the lock, 28/60 without it, same host, same load).

Concurrency was exercised through the real subagent_stop_validate.py as a subprocess pair with both stdins written before either stdout was read, so the children are genuinely concurrent (the failure mode the round-2 review found in an earlier fixture).

findings.statement: Obligation 2 (receipt/lease creation failure is a hard Start failure) is DISCHARGED on HEAD 4305533, including the round-7 defect. The two round-7 reproductions are closed and I confirmed both closures by mutation rather than by reading the code's own account of itself. (a) UNCONDITIONAL EVALUATION: `describe_admission_receipt` (subagent_start_context.py:475-585) calls `classify_receipt_matches` (:529) and then `orphaned_mints` (:533-535) with no gate; the ledger read at :514-527 is guarded only by `ledger_path.is_file()`. Mutation M5 restored the round-6 `if (not matches) and ledger_path.is_file():` gating and was killed by test_subagentstart_hard_fails_when_a_valid_receipt_masks_an_orphaned_mint AND by the false-positive control's own second half. (b) THE PER-ASSIGNMENT QUALIFICATION IS CORRECT, NOT MERELY PRESENT -- this was the specific risk to check, and I probed it directly rather than trusting the fixture. Ten scenarios against HEAD bytes in scratch trees: healthy two-agent run with BOTH mints open -> PASS for each admitted agent and PASS for an unregistered helper; reopened chain (minted for g1, reopened for g2) -> PASS for the new agent, PASS for the superseded agent, PASS for a bystander; an open mint naming this agent in a DIFFERENT (non-active) run -> PASS, the check is active-run-scoped on both the receipt directory and the ledger; healthy token-only mint whose receipt landed -> PASS; an orphaned mint naming g1 -> FAIL for g1 and PASS for the unrelated admitted g2; fresh run with nothing minted -> PASS. No false positive was found on the agent-keyed arm. Mutation M9 (drop the `assignment_id != admitted_assignment_id` exclusion in the direction that clears everything once the agent holds any receipt) was killed; mutation M6 (return no orphans) and M8 (report the orphan but strip it from `errors`) each killed all seven Start-orphan fixtures, so the check is load-bearing in `Hook preflight: PASS|FAIL` and not merely printed. (c) TOKEN-ONLY ARM REACHABLE AND SCOPED HONESTLY: `--agent-id-unknown` writes `expected_agent_id: ""`, so `orphaned_mints` handles it in a separate run-scoped arm keyed on 'did this mint produce a receipt file at all' (:402-406). Mutation M7 (delete the arm) was killed by both token-only fixtures. I reproduced the stated over-breadth (probe P8): a token-only mint whose receipt write failed makes Start FAIL for a healthy, correctly admitted agent elsewhere in the same run. That is over-broad WITHIN the run, exactly as the module docstring (:117-148) says, and its three stated justifications hold on inspection -- the row only survives receipt-less when the receipt write actually failed, `admit_agent.py` then exits non-zero and prints no token, and a successful re-mint self-clears. (d) MALFORMED/UNREADABLE LEDGER IS A FAIL, NOT A SKIP: probes P4 and P9 returned FAIL for both the receipt-holding agent and a bystander; mutation M10 (silently drop a malformed line) was killed. (e) LEASE HALF unchanged and still fail-closed (:665-677). RESIDUAL I AM STATING RATHER THAN GLOSSING, because it is the one shape that still reaches `Hook preflight: PASS`: if the LEDGER append fails (I reproduced this with `chmod 0o500` on `.agent-harness/runs/<run>/`), `admit_agent.py` exits 1 with an EMPTY stdout and no token, no ledger row and no receipt exist, and Start reports 'none found' / PASS. This is NOT the round-6/round-7 defect (there the intent record existed and Start passed anyway); here nothing on disk distinguishes the case from an unregistered helper agent, no ADMISSION_TOKEN was ever emitted so no agent can be spawned bound to it, and Stop refuses any result without an open receipt. I verified the empty stdout and rc=1 directly, which is precisely the compensating-control claim the audit report makes -- and unlike the claim it retracted at round 6, this one is true.
assumptions_used: Start is advisory relative to Stop by design: it reads only, and Stop performs the authoritative consume. I judged Start's verdict on whether it is load-bearing in `Hook preflight`, which the result contract's `subagent_start_preflight: "PASS"` requirement makes true in practice.

findings.statement: Obligation 3 (same-run substitution and receipt-write-failure negative fixtures) is DISCHARGED on HEAD 4305533, and the fixtures are non-vacuous by mutation. Suite: 161 collected, 161 passed (106 in test_hooks.py, up from 102 at a9db6b2 -- I confirmed both counts from the git objects, so the 102 -> 106 claim is verified, not taken). I applied 16 single-anchor mutants to a scratch MIRROR of .codex and .agent-harness (the live tree was never modified), ran the full test_hooks.py after each, and reverted: ALL 16 WERE KILLED, each by an on-topic, correctly named fixture. THE RECEIPT-WRITE FIXTURE IS REAL AND ISOLATES THE RIGHT WRITE: test_admit_agent_fails_closed_when_the_receipt_cannot_be_written uses `_mint_with_unwritable_receipt_dir`, which chmods `.agent-harness/admissions/<run>` to 0o500 while leaving `.agent-harness/runs/<run>` writable -- so the ledger append succeeds and only `dump_json_atomic` fails. It asserts the split explicitly (ledger row present, receipt absent, no `.tmp.*` residue, stderr names the receipt and not the ledger, stdout empty and token-free). M12 (swallow the receipt-write OSError) and M13 (write the receipt before the ledger) both killed it. This is the fixture that round 6 proved did not exist; it exists, and it fails when the behaviour it names is removed. SAME-RUN SUBSTITUTION: test_subagentstop_blocks_same_run_assignment_substitution is killed by M16 (disable the token-digest compare). THE NEWEST FOUR (added at 5c474d0) ARE EACH TWO-SIDED: masks_an_orphaned_mint carries an in-test control that consumes the orphan and re-asserts PASS on the same tree; passes_when_the_open_mint_is_the_receipt_it_holds carries a control that relocates the receipt to a different assignment and re-asserts FAIL -- which is why M5 and M9 kill it and not only the positive fixture; hard_fails_on_an_unattributable_token_only_mint re-runs with a second agent_id to pin the run-scope over-breadth as intended rather than accidental; clears_a_token_only_mint_that_produced_a_receipt deletes the receipt and re-asserts FAIL. An AST sweep of test_hooks.py found no test function with zero assertions (minimum 2). NOT CLAIMED: 16 mutants over 106 fixtures is a sample, not exhaustive mutation coverage; the sample was chosen to hit the specific guards the four obligations rest on.

findings.statement: Obligation 4 (a replacement live overlapping-run canary with unique write attribution) is DISCHARGED on HEAD 4305533. C6 IS NOT STALE, which is where its three predecessors died: the artifact pins stop_hook_sha256 0533da88... and start_hook_sha256 af8f7016..., and I recomputed BOTH against HEAD -- both match exactly. The window is closed structurally as well as by digest: C6 ran at commit d564821 (21:38:50 +0900) and was sealed by 4305533 (21:47:02 +0900), and `git diff --stat d564821..HEAD` shows the only changes are the canary's own run artifacts -- no hook, script or test byte moved under it. LIVE: the C6 result is a real 3-finding review of the actual hook code written between 12:39:20Z and 12:45:14Z, its Start hook really ran (raw_logs/start_out.json is a 27 KB injected context reading 'Active run: run-...-canary-c6' and 'Admission receipt: open, bound to assignment A-D070-CANARY-C6'), and stop_out.json is zero bytes, i.e. the Stop hook emitted no block. OVERLAPPING: the decoy run directory exists with a RUN_PLAN created 12:40:24Z -- after the canary's 12:39:14Z mint and Start -- so the pointer theft is mid-flight, and the pointer named the decoy at BOTH ends of a 36 ms bracket (12:46:32.570862531Z / 12:46:32.606719483Z) around the dispatch. That is independently corroborated by a differently-authored artifact: the canary agent's own result, written at 12:45 before the stop, records '.agent-harness/ACTIVE_RUN currently reads run-20260729-f10-d070-canary-c6-decoy' from a direct read. UNIQUE WRITE ATTRIBUTION, verified on live bytes today: the consume row and the receipt both name agent_id d070-canary-c6 with expected_agent_id enforced, and pin result_sha256 sha256:66b5fb3c... which I recomputed against the result file on disk -- it still matches; assignment_sha256 sha256:8ceeb1ec... likewise matches, and the lease records the same run_id and the same sealed assignment digest. THE BRACKET ESTABLISHES WHAT OBLIGATION 4 ASKS: the property at issue is that the Stop bound the run from the Start-time lease while the mutable pointer named a different run for the whole dispatch. The bracket surrounds the process lifetime, so the pointer state is pinned across the consume rather than merely before it -- the exact defect C4 was rejected for. THE SECOND-RESOLUTION LIMITATION IS HONEST, NOT EVASIVE: `consumed_at` is stamped `timespec='seconds'` (subagent_stop_validate.py:687), so sub-second ordering genuinely cannot be proven from it, the artifact says so in as many words, and it does not need to -- the consume happens inside the bracketed process by construction, so the second-resolution stamp is a corroborating cross-check, not the load-bearing evidence. Recording the limit rather than asserting containment is the correct call. NOT ESTABLISHED: that the bracket was taken 'in one shell command with no intervening work' is the writer's assertion; there is no shell transcript. It is corroborated by the 36 ms width, by stop_out.json's mtime, and by the ledger consume falling in the same wall second, but it is attestation, not proof.
assumptions_used: The retained stop_event.json shows `admission_proof` already replaced by its digest, which is scrub_admission_proof.py operating as designed; the real token is therefore not re-verifiable from evidence, but the receipt's and the ledger row's token_digest agree with each other.

findings.statement: The D-067 audit report -- docs/audit/BD622_D067_admission_binding_2026-07-29.md, a required input to this review and the document §5 nominates as the D-070 adjudicator's evidence -- does NOT match the code at HEAD 4305533 on two of the four obligations under adjudication. This is the fourth instance of this chain's own named failure mode, inverted: the record is now BEHIND the mechanism rather than ahead of it. Its only edit at the round-7 commit 5c474d0 was the string '102 pass' -> '106 pass'; I diffed it. Specifics, each verified against current bytes: (1) OBLIGATION 4 IS MISDIRECTED. §2 line 128 says '**C5 replaces it**, run against frozen bytes at commit d94270f' and details C5 as the standing overlapping-run canary. C5 pins stop_hook_sha256 dc19da4d..., which is not HEAD (0533da88...); the project's own VALIDATION_LEDGER row for round 7 says so explicitly. C6, which IS current and which I verified in F-R8-04, appears nowhere in the report, and §4's 'Live canaries' table still lists only C1/C2/C3 -- no C4, C5 or C6. An adjudicator reading this report for obligation 4 is pointed at a canary the project has already declared stale. (2) OBLIGATION 2 IS MISDESCRIBED. §2's 'Start now distinguishes **three** states rather than two' (lines 195-214) is the round-6 rule. The shipped rule is different in two ways I reproduced: the ledger consultation is per-assignment (an orphan is cleared only by an admitting receipt for that same assignment), and there is a run-scoped token-only arm under which a receipt-less `--agent-id-unknown` row hard-FAILs EVERY agent starting into that run -- including a healthy, correctly admitted one (probe P8). Neither appears in the report. The over-breadth is an operational hazard disclosed in code and in the commit message but not in the audit record. (3) OBLIGATION 1'S MECHANISM IS UNRECORDED. `grep -i 'lock|flock|concurren|per-run'` over the whole report returns no hit naming the per-(run, agent_id) consume lock, the round-6 finding that O_EXCL alone admitted both stops in 126/200 trials, or the per-run scope of the binding. §2's table row 75 still reads 'Concurrent double consume | silent overwrite | `O_EXCL`, one attribution row'. The outcome claim is true on current bytes; the mechanism attribution is the pre-round-6 one, i.e. the description under which that defect hid. (4) A DANGLING CROSS-REFERENCE: line 110 says 'its fixes and the retraction above are recorded in the round-6 correction' -- there is no round-6 correction section; §2 has round-4 and round-5 corrections only. (5) §3, the section titled 'Review record', reads 'four rounds, all FAIL' and 'took four passes to stabilise'; seven rounds have completed, and round 7 appears nowhere in the report. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: it is not a mechanism defect -- F-R8-01 through F-R8-04 are all pass, and the fix is a documentation update, not a code change. It is also not a case of the project having no accurate record: docs/harness/VALIDATION_LEDGER.md's round-7 row and the 5c474d0 commit message are both current and candid, and the C6 artifact is self-describing. But the audit report is the artifact this review was told to check against the code, it is the artifact a gate decision would be read from, and on obligations 2 and 4 it would mislead that decision today. Given that three of the defects in this chain were in the record rather than the code, I am recording this as a fail rather than an advisory.
assumptions_used: I treat the audit report as a record surface whose accuracy is in scope, because the assignment lists it in required_inputs and the review question asks what is established versus asserted. I do not treat it as a mechanism defect and have not let it affect the four obligation verdicts.

unresolved: Whether a gate flip should be blocked on a record defect when the mechanism is established is an adjudication question, not mine. My position is stated: the four mechanism obligations are individually discharged on current bytes; the audit report is not a faithful description of them.

The same-OS-user residual stands and is out of scope as a finding. My judgement is that it does not prevent honest discharge of these four items, because none of the four claims forgery resistance and the residual is stated in three places I checked (admit_agent.py module docstring, .agent-harness/README.md:58, and the report's own table row). Discharge would become dishonest only if some surface began claiming more than confusion-class protection; none does.
